methods: Group project of three or four
teaching_methods.additional_notes: The courses provide a theoretical understanding of the functioning of large language models (LLM) and RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) architectures, relying on concrete use cases to illustrate their implementation. The tutorials take the form of practical workshops in Python, allowing students to gradually build a red thread project integrating data extraction, creation of a conversational architecture, and development of a test interface. Case studies complement the practical approach, through critical analysis of real deployments of generative AI. These sequences open up reflection on issues related to algorithmic biases, the reliability of generated content, and the usage limits of these technologies.

topics: Introduction to language models: review of transformer architectures, attention mechanism, notion of tokens, overview of libraries (OpenAI, open alternatives)
In-depth LangChain: structure, sequential management and application to conversation, creation of a multi-step responding agent
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation): principles, integration of document retrieval mechanisms in the pipeline, mention of LLaMa Index
Discovery of LangGraph: construction of agent graphs, interaction between multiple automated "nodes", concrete use cases
Practice on concrete cases: deployment of a mini-customer service, customization of responses, management of a vector store (vector document base)
Restricted production deployment: use of OpenAI token, best optimization practices, ethical issues and LLM limits

external: Basic knowledge in machine learning (ML), particularly in regression and classification
Familiarity with data science libraries (numpy, pandas, possibly scikit-learn)

learning_outcomes: Explain the fundamentals of transformer-type language models (attention mechanisms, concept of "tokens", ...)
Implement a generative AI pipeline (including sequence management via LangChain)
Integrate RAG techniques (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) to make responses more relevant
Design and organize a graph of agents (LangGraph) collaborating to handle complex tasks (customer service, search engines, etc.)
Deploy a generative AI application in restricted production (PoC) using OpenAI libraries, while managing token consumption
Identify ethical issues and best practices related to the deployment of generative AI applications
